title: Request Scribe — Annotated Customer Journeys and Prototype Buckets
content:
Executive summary:
This doc stitches together ~40 customer touchpoints captured between 2025-04 and 2025-06 (support tickets, sales calls, SRE incidents, and in-product feedback). Goal: produce pragmatic, prototype-level responses (3 lanes) with clear owner recommendations and ROI proxies so product/engineering can pick lowest-risk pilots.

Signal provenance (condensed):
- Support tickets (17): common theme — subtle latency regressions when using model variants across routes; customers report silent fallbacks in middle of sessions -> workaround: restart session or pin model.
- Sales/AE feedback (9): asks for better capacity guarantees for bursty workloads, clearer cost forecasting when routing across "economy" vs "performance" variants.
- SRE incidents (4): two incidents show cache-coherency issues after model rollouts (prefix cache invalidation not propagated); root-cause traced to rollout script not bumping cache key namespace.
- In-product feedback / usage telemetry (10): repeated pattern where customers circumvent streaming by issuing short polling requests to keep tokens deterministic.

Representative quotes (verbatim):
- "We had a 30-min window where completions returned wrong model behavior — hard to trace in logs, our app just degrades." — enterprise-cust-17
- "It'd be great if the API told us which model variant actually served the request and why fallback happened." — platform team, fintech
- "Price spikes during month-end batches killed our forecast. We need a predictable budget knob." — AI-native startup

Workaround motifs we observed:
- Pin-to-version at SDK layer (popular, but brittle across latency regressions)
- Local prefix caching in client (some customers implement to avoid repeated prompt tokens)
- Short-polling to emulate streaming (increases request rate and cost)

Prototype buckets (3 lanes, ordered by expected adoption & feedback urgency):
A) Transparent Serving Debug Layer (short-term, 2-3 sprints):
  - What: API response includes "served_variant" + fallback_reason + rollout_id. Optional header for telemetry ingestion.
  - Why: reduces investigation time for CS/SE and customers; addresses "which model served" ask.
  - Effort: S
  - Risks: exposing internal names may leak variant semantics — provide mapping or anonymized ids.
  - Owner: eng-platform (traceability) + cs (customer messaging)
  - ROI proxy: reduce investigation hours by 30% for reported incidents; quicker escalation resolution.

B) Budgetable Routing Profiles (mid-term, 1 quarter):
  - What: Route profiles customers can opt into (guaranteed-cost ceiling, priority-latency, spot-saver). SDK + Console + API flags.
  - Why: addresses unpredictable billing and cost-spike asks; product lever to upsell dedicated capacity.
  - Effort: M-L (infra + billing + console)
  - UX note: Console exposes simulated monthly spend given token distribution.
  - Owner: product-hosted-api + finance
  - ROI proxy: conversion of 8% of mid-market customers to reserved commits; reduction in billing disputes.

C) Rollout-safe Prefix Cache Protocol (longer-term, 2 quarters):
  - What: Explicit cache namespace and rollout-aware invalidation primitives (server-side and SDK hooks).
  - Why: prevents coherency incidents and client workarounds; reduces cold-start token costs.
  - Effort: L
  - Risks: requires coordination across runtimes and private deployments.
  - Owner: serving-runtime + private-deployments
  - ROI proxy: decrease in SRE incident MTTR; token-cost reduction for high-reuse workloads.

Low-effort/high-impact patches (quick wins):
- Add telemetry tag to streaming fallback events (owners: observability; Effort: XS)
- Document recommended "pinning" pattern with caveats and example SDK helper (owner: devx; Effort: S)
- Temporary SDK flag: force-label served_variant in responses for debugging (owner: devx; Effort: XS)

Open questions & unresolved tradeoffs:
- How much internal variant information is safe to reveal before it becomes an ops surface? (security/product risk)
- Budgetable profiles: what SLAs back a "guaranteed-cost ceiling"? Do we limit throughput or throttle? (legal/finance implications)
- Rollout cache protocol: can private deployments adopt without changing customer infra? (compatibility)

Next steps (owners + due dates):
- Align on A prototype spec and minimal schema for "served_variant" by 2025-06-20 — owner: Evan Rivera
- Console mock for Budgetable Routing by 2025-07-10 — owner: Priya Natarajan
- Internal runbook for pinning + customer-facing KB article draft by 2025-06-25 — owner: Maya Chen
- Spike: cache invalidation test harness for serving-runtime by 2025-07-15 — owner: Tomás Alvarez

Tracking metrics suggestion (minimal set):
- % of incidents with "served_variant" missing in investigation notes (goal -> 0%)
- Monthly count of fallback events per customer (baseline + trend)
- Billing dispute volume related to routing/cost predictions

Appendix: sample ticket excerpts (anonymized), quick CLI examples for prototype A, and links to related PRs and runbooks.

Notes-to-self / things to surface in Friday sync:
- Ask infra team for sample rollout ids and their current naming scheme
- Coordinate with legal on acceptable telemetry exposures
- Suggest running a 1-week pilot where 5 trusted customers opt into the debug header

End of doc.
